examples.en: All my clothes are in the wardrobe.

examples.sr: Купили смо нови [шифо̀њер] за спаваћу собу.
examples.en: We bought a new wardrobe for the bedroom.
The child collected pine cones in the forest.
Golden pine cones hang on the fir tree.
How much does a woman's haircut cost?
Book a haircut for Saturday.
The girl has long bangs.
She wears her hair with bangs.

note: usually plural

examples.en: Hundreds of bats live in the cave.
A bat sleeps upside down.
We ordered grilled shrimp.
The shrimp risotto is excellent.
Her father is a well-educated man.
We are looking for trained staff.
She is studying in Belgrade.
My father got his education abroad.

note: implies studying over several years

examples.en: The door has been creaking for a year.
The snow crunches underfoot.
Don't be stingy with the guests.
He is known as a miser.
The child swims with a swim ring.
Inflate the ring before you swim.

note: colloquial, from German

examples.en: In the morning I wear a robe and drink coffee.
I bought a soft robe.

note: from German; a pool robe is «баде-мантил»

examples.en: Zip up your fly before you go out.
The skirt has a slit at the back.

note: colloquial

examples.en: Grandpa had a stroke last week.

examples.sr: После [шло̀га] му је тешко да говори.
examples.en: After the stroke he has trouble speaking.

note: colloquial; the formal term is «мождани удар»

examples.en: This salami has a strange taste.
That apartment has its own charm.

note: colloquial, from German

examples.sr: Он је прави [шме̏кер], све девојке га воле.
examples.en: He's a real charmer, all the girls love him.
The neighbor dresses like a dandy.

note: colloquial; not necessarily rich

examples.sr: Она је права [шмѐкерка], зна шта хоће.
examples.en: She's a real operator, she knows what she wants.

examples.sr: Не верујем тој [шмѐкерки], све ради из интереса.
examples.en: I don't trust that smooth operator, she does everything out of self-interest.

note: colloquial; the feminine of «шмекер», can also sound slightly ironic

forms: шминкам се, шминкају се; pf. нашминкати се

examples.en: She always puts on makeup before going out.

examples.sr: Не волим да се [шми̏нкам] сваког дана.
examples.en: I don't like wearing makeup every day.

examples.sr: [Шми̏нкер] је дошао сат времена пре венчања.
examples.en: The makeup artist came an hour before the wedding.
I called a makeup artist for the prom.
Sand the board with sandpaper.
Buy finer sandpaper.
I've been sniffling all day because of a cold.
Stop sniffling and blow your nose.
The girl has a blue clip in her hair.
I lost my hair clip.
A good tailor made my suit.
Grandpa was a tailor in town.

note: colloquial, from German

examples.en: Don't wolf it down so fast, you'll choke.

examples.sr: Он [шо̑па̄] хамбургер као да му је последњи.
examples.en: He's gobbling that hamburger as if it were his last.

note: colloquial

examples.en: In summer I wear shorts and a T-shirt.
I bought blue shorts.
A stone damaged the windshield.
Scrape the ice off the windshield.

note: colloquial

examples.en: Apply the putty with a putty knife.
Wash the putty knife after work.
She pinned the fabric in place.
Find me a pin.
The shelf is made of plywood.
We bought thin plywood for the cabinet.

note: from German; in everyday speech often just «шпер»

examples.en: Grandpa took out a deck of cards.
Who is going to shuffle the deck?

note: usually «шпил карата»

examples.en: It's crowded downtown at rush hour.
I avoid driving at rush hour.

note: «у шпицу» means at rush hour; a German loanword

examples.en: Cook the soup on the stove.
Turn off the stove before you leave.
The nurse took a new syringe.
Every syringe is used only once.

note: colloquially also wine with soda water

examples.en: I'll order a spritzer with ice.
In summer I like a cold spritzer.

note: white wine and soda water; with mineral water it is «гемишт»

examples.en: Tighten that screw.
One screw is missing.
Hand me the screwdriver, please.
You open the lid with this screwdriver.
Sorrel soup is sour.
Sorrel grows in the garden.

note: rarely used in Serbian cooking

examples.en: After the surgery he walked on crutches.

examples.sr: Дај ми [шта̏ке], не могу сам да станем.
examples.en: Give me the crutches, I can't stand up by myself.

note: usually plural: «штаке»

examples.sr: Сломио је ногу и сада хода на [шта̀кама].
examples.en: He broke his leg and now walks on crutches.
Bring me my crutches, please.
There's no paper in the printer.
We bought a new printer.
He set up the easel by the window.
The students took their easels to the park.
I want to open a savings account.
The interest on savings deposits is low.
My father is very thrifty.
Let's be sparing with water.
Saving water is important in summer.
His savings are spent.
They found his stash under the floor.
I have a stash for money.

note: colloquial, 1990s slang

examples.sr: Он је велика [штѐкара] и никад не троши.
examples.en: He's a big skinflint and never spends anything.
Don't be a skinflint, buy yourself something.

note: colloquial; from «штек», a stash or savings

examples.en: Smoking is harmful to your health.
Such a habit is harmful.

note: not to be confused with «вредан» (hardworking)

examples.sr: Не могу дуго да ходам у [шти̏клама].
examples.en: I can't walk in heels for long.
She put on a dress and heels.
Hang the laundry on the line with clothespins.
I need one more clothespin.
The coach times it with a stopwatch.
I started a stopwatch on my phone.

meanings: city beach (on a river or lake)

examples.en: We're going to the beach by the river.
There are quite a lot of people at the beach.

note: a river or lake beach such as Ada Ciganlija; you go «на штранд»

examples.en: I bought a T-shirt with blue stripes.
He wears a striped shirt.

note: usually plural: «на штрафте» means striped

examples.en: Grandma loves to knit sweaters.
I learned to knit a scarf.

note: colloquial; «плести» is the standard word

examples.en: Grandma is making walnut strudel.
Have a piece of apple strudel.
A book is sticking out of the bag.
He always stands out in a group.
I've been hiccuping for half an hour.
The baby hiccups after milk.
Grandpa wears a fur hat in winter.
The new hat is made of fur.

note: also a traditional men's fur cap

examples.en: This old oak is hollow.
That's just empty talk.

note: «шупља прича» means empty talk

examples.en: My brother-in-law lives in Belgrade.
I go fishing with my brother-in-law.
The kids are kicking a ball around the yard.
It's not nice to kick other people.

note: «шутка» is slang for a mosh pit at rock concerts

examples.en: The boys are kicking a ball in the yard.
Don't kick it toward the window!
Leaves rustle underfoot.
Something is rustling in the grass.
My neighbor is a real oddball.
He's acting like a goofball.

note: colloquial, affectionately teasing; a grown-up who acts like a kid

examples.en: The cat is stalking a mouse.
Don't sneak around the house at night.
I have to slog away even on Saturdays.
He toils all day at the construction site.

note: colloquial; of a machine: to work properly

examples.sr: Не желим да се мешам са тим [шља̑мом].
examples.en: I don't want to mix with that scum.
Some riffraff is sitting over there.

note: rude, offensive

examples.en: Ripe plums fall from the tree.
Rakija is made from plums.

tips: «Суве шљиве» are prunes, «суво грожђе» is raisins. Fresh plums are used to make the brandy шљивовица.

examples.en: Grandpa keeps good slivovitz for guests.
Slivovitz is the best-known Serbian rakija.
The dress is covered in sequins.
The kids are gluing glitter onto a card.

note: always plural

examples.sr: На овој плажи је [шљу́нак], не песак.
examples.en: This beach has pebbles, not sand.
Walking on pebbles hurts.
The cat curled up in the corner.

examples.sr: Од хладноће сам се [шћућу̀рио] у капуту.
examples.en: I huddled up in my coat from the cold.
Every pupil has a notebook.
He was the best student of his year.
Grandma made us a real treat.
The kids came for a treat.

note: colloquial

examples.en: Buy me a sesame bagel.
A warm bagel is best for breakfast.
The soles of the shoes are worn out.
Take the boots in to get new soles.
Plants need fertilizer once a month.
We bought organic fertilizer.

meanings: djuvec (casserole of rice, vegetables and meat)

examples.sr: Мама прави [ђу̀веч] са пиринчем и месом.
examples.en: Mom makes djuvec with rice and meat.
Djuvec is baked in the oven.

note: a dish of Balkan cuisine

examples.en: Tea with ginger helps with a cold.
Cut up a little ginger.
Lily of the valley blooms in May.
The scent of lily of the valley is wonderful.
On St. George's Day many families celebrate their slava.
Real summer arrives after St. George's Day.

note: the traditional boundary between winter and summer

examples.en: We danced all evening to the band.
Stop jumping around the room!

note: colloquial

examples.en: There's chaos in that office.
I won't tolerate sloppiness at work.

note: colloquial, from Turkish

forms: јавим се, јаве се; impf. јављати се

examples.en: I called my parents.
Why don't you get in touch with the boss?

note: + dat.; «јави се» also means "call me"

examples.en: The autumn color of a maple is red.
The guitar is made of maple.
She has high cheekbones.
He felt the pulse with his fingertips.
Her cheeks turned red from the cold.
He touched the paper with his fingertips.
White lambs graze in the meadow.
The shepherd guards the lambs from the wolf.

note: a collective noun in -ад

examples.en: Lamb is eaten at Easter.
Lamb on a spit is a specialty.
What misery!
They live in great hardship.

examples.sr: Наш [јазавѝчар] воли да копа по башти.
examples.en: Our dachshund likes to dig in the garden.

examples.sr: [Јазавѝчар] има кратке ноге и дуго тело.
examples.en: A dachshund has short legs and a long body.

note: from «јазавац» (badger): a dog bred for hunting badgers

examples.en: We wear flip-flops at the beach.
I left my flip-flops at home.
A little kid is jumping in the meadow.
The shepherd is tending the kids on the hill.
The chair is made of ash.
An ash tree grows by the road.
The baby has gone to daycare since the fall.
The nursery is open until five o'clock.

note: plural only

examples.sr: Беба иде у [ја̀слице] од једне године.
examples.en: The baby has gone to daycare since turning one.

examples.sr: У нашем граду нема довољно места у [ја̀слицама].
examples.en: There aren't enough places in the nurseries in our town.

note: plural only; for children under 3

examples.en: The cat has soft pads on its paws.
Put a small cushion behind your back.
The pillowcase needs to be changed.
I have two white pillowcases.
The eel lives in rivers and in the sea.
Smoked eel is a delicacy.
The word is in the singular.

examples.sr: Глагол је у [једнѝни], а именица у множини.
examples.en: The verb is singular and the noun is plural.
I like plain clothes.
The wall is a solid color.
This is a one-way street.
You can't go this way, the road is one-way.
We're looking for a one-room apartment downtown.
This apartment is one-room and bright.

note: «једноипособан» is an apartment of one and a half rooms

examples.en: This summer I'm learning to sail.
Sailing depends on the wind.
Food passes through the esophagus.
I have a burning feeling in my esophagus.
A hedgehog lives in the garden.
When a hedgehog gets scared, it curls into a ball.

forms: јежим се, јеже се; pf. најежити се

examples.en: I get goosebumps when I hear that song.
The children shivered from the cold.

note: јежити се од + gen.

examples.en: Fear sends a shiver through me.
I have a fever and chills.

note: «пролази ме језа» means a shiver runs through me

examples.en: Tall firs grow in the forest.
The fir is an evergreen tree.

note: not to be confused with «јело» (dish)

examples.en: The girl put on an embroidered vest.
He wears a leather vest over his shirt.
Last fall we moved to Belgrade.
I started learning Serbian last fall.

note: usually about the fall that has just passed

examples.en: Fall days are short.
I wear a fall jacket.
This mushroom is edible.
Not all berries are edible.

examples.sr: Моја [јѐтрва] и ја живимо у истој згради.
examples.en: My sister-in-law and I live in the same building.
The brothers' wives often see each other at the slava.

note: a rare word, but alive in large families

examples.en: Beer is made from barley.
They sowed barley in the field.
In winter I sleep under a thick quilt.
Grandma sewed a new quilt.

note: «ћебе» is a light blanket, «јорган» a quilted or down comforter

examples.en: Lilacs smell wonderful in May.
He brought her a bouquet of lilacs.
The main heroine of the novel is a young teacher.

examples.sr: Деца воле ту [јуна̀кињу] из цртаног филма.
examples.en: Children love that heroine from the cartoon.
Their heroism is remembered.
He received a medal for valor.
I use young beef for goulash.
Young beef is more tender than regular beef.

note: meat of cattle 12-24 months old

examples.en: Yippee, we're going to the seaside!
Yay! I passed the exam!
Don't trust that slimeball.

examples.sr: Он је прави [љига̀вац], лако се извуче.
examples.en: He's a real slippery customer, he always wriggles out of things.

note: colloquial

examples.en: There's a white lily on the table.
I like the scent of lilies.
Two young people are kissing on the bench.
They kiss goodbye.
She wore a purple dress.
At dusk the sky was violet.
The first violet blooms in March.
The scent of violets is delicate.
There are a lot of people in the park.
Good people always help.

note: the plural of «човек»

examples.en: Crack the eggshell.
Fish have scales.
I spread ljutenica on my bread.

examples.sr: Бака прави [љутѐницу] од паприке и парадајза.
examples.en: Grandma makes ljutenica from peppers and tomatoes.

note: a spicy spread with peppers and garlic, similar to ajvar

examples.en: Peel the potatoes with a peeler.
Where is the vegetable peeler?
I'm peeling potatoes for lunch.
My skin is peeling after the sun.
A mother rocks her baby in her arms.
The children are swinging on the swing.
The children are swinging on the swings.
The boat is rocking on the waves.

note: figuratively: to waver, to be unstable
tips: To swing, for example on a swing: «љуљати се на љуљашци». Figuratively it means to waver or to be shaky.

examples.en: The child is playing on the swing.
There's a new swing in the park.
Grandpa sows corn in the field.
There are fields and meadows around the house.

examples.sr: Цео дан само [њо̀паш] и гледаш серије.
examples.en: All day you just stuff your face and watch TV series.
Don't pig out on so many sweets.

note: colloquial, eating without measure

examples.sr: Ко ми је [ћа̏пио] оловку са стола?
examples.en: Who swiped my pen from the desk?
He snatched the last piece of pie.

note: colloquial; petty theft

examples.en: We chatted on the phone for hours.
I like to chat with the neighbors.

examples.sr: Уз кафу је дошло и пријатно [ћа̏ска̄ње].
examples.en: Pleasant small talk came along with the coffee.
Chatting is not allowed in class.
Tonight we're eating at a ćevapi place.
The best ćevapi place is near the market.
We ordered five ćevapi and a lepinja.
The ćevapi are on the grill.

note: usually plural; diminutive ћевапчићи

examples.en: We ordered a portion of ćevapi.
I like ćevapi with onions.

note: mostly plural; the singular is ћевап

examples.en: We ordered a portion of ćevapčići.
Ćevapčići are served with onions.

note: usually plural

examples.en: My father is already starting to go bald.
I'm not balding yet, thank God.
The pendant is made of amber.
They sell amber jewelry.
Grandma wove a kilim.
An old kilim hangs on the wall.

note: a Turkish word; usually a flat-woven rug without pile

examples.en: At school we learn Cyrillic and Latin script.
This inscription is written in Cyrillic.
A wolf changes its coat, but never its nature.
He has a difficult temper.
We need charcoal for the grill.
I bought a bag of charcoal.
Grandma keeps honey in a clay pot.
We bought an old pot at the market.
The old bridge on the Drina is famous.
We crossed the stone bridge.

note: literary, dated; in everyday speech «мост»

examples.en: He doesn't eat red meat, only turkey.
A turkey sandwich is light.
For Christmas we made a stuffed turkey.
This is a turkey from a farm.

note: the meat is «ћуретина»

examples.en: He is a quiet, taciturn man.
My sister is quiet.
Mom made meatballs with mashed potatoes.

examples.sr: [Ћу̀фте] у парадајз сосу су моје омиљено јело.
examples.en: Meatballs in tomato sauce are my favorite dish.

note: mostly plural: «ћуфте»

examples.en: What are you two whispering about over there?
The girls whispered all evening.
Admission was free.
You're wasting your breath on him, he won't listen.

note: colloquial, a Turkish loanword; often «за џабе»

examples.en: That freeloader lives at other people's expense.
I don't want to feed a freeloader.

note: colloquial, jocular or contemptuous

examples.en: He is carrying a sack of potatoes.
There is cement in the sack.

note: «купити мачку у џаку» means to buy a pig in a poke

examples.en: There is an old mosque in the town.
We visited the mosque in Novi Pazar.

examples.sr: Дете целе вечери [џа̀нгриза] јер је уморно.
examples.en: The child has been fussing all evening because he's tired.

examples.sr: Престани да [џа̀нгризаш] и реци шта ти смета.
examples.en: Stop whining and tell me what's bothering you.

note: «џангризало» is a person who is always grumbling

examples.en: Come on, darling, sit next to me.
Darling, you mean everything to me.

note: a Turkish loanword, an affectionate form of address

examples.en: Coffee is brewed in a džezva.
Take the džezva off the stove.

note: a copper pot for Turkish-style coffee; a Turkish word

examples.en: Mom gives me an allowance every week.
They got pocket money for the trip.
Watch out for pickpockets on the bus.
A pickpocket stole my wallet.
He dressed like a real lout.

examples.sr: Не волим да се дружим са [џѝберима].
examples.en: I don't like hanging out with louts.

note: slang, derogatory

examples.en: We ordered a gigantic pizza.
They were building a gigantic tower.
Your room is full of knickknacks.

examples.sr: Баба чува све те [џи̏џабиџе] у фиоци.
examples.en: Grandma keeps all those trinkets in a drawer.

note: colloquial, a jocular word for a heap of small things

examples.en: Take the mop and wipe the floor.
The mop is behind the door.

note: false friend: not a jogger but a floor mop

examples.en: In the morning I mop the kitchen.
He likes to jog by the river.

note: colloquial, two meanings: to mop the floor and to jog

examples.sr: У тој игри [џо̀кер] може да замени сваку карту.
examples.en: In that game a joker can replace any card.
He drew the joker and laughed.
What a vicious cur, it wants to bite everyone!
The neighbors' mutt barks all the time.

note: pejorative

meanings: the guest's reply to «Добро дошли!»: glad to be here
forms: literally: better that we found you

examples.en: - Welcome! - Glad to be here!

note: A polite reply of a guest to the hosts. A simple «Хвала!» works too.

meanings: a gossip, a person who spreads unverified rumors

examples.en: You're a real gossip.

note: Mileva is a common female name; the phrase is used for men too.

meanings: a greeting to the host on the day of his family's slava

examples.en: Happy slava, neighbor!

note: Slava is the day of a family's patron saint. The most widely celebrated one is «Никољдан», December 19.

meanings: no problem, don't worry, nothing to fret about

examples.en: - Will you help me? - No problem.

note: A colloquial phrase. Literally it can also mean "there are no cold spells", but it is mostly used as "everything is fine".

key: phr:ко рано рани, две среће граби
meanings: the early bird catches the worm
forms: literally: whoever rises early grabs two pieces of luck

examples.sr: Устани раније, [ко̏ ра̏но ра̏ни, две̑ сре̏ће гра̏би].
examples.en: Get up earlier: the early bird catches the worm.

note: A proverb. «рани» is from «ранити» (to get up early), «граби» from «грабити» (to grab).

meanings: to stick one's nose into other people's business
forms: literally: to meddle in other people's affairs

examples.sr: Не волим да се [ме̏шам у ту̀ђа по̀сла].
examples.en: I don't like to meddle in other people's business.

note: The form «посла» (not «послови») is used only in set phrases.

forms: literally: to look at one's own affairs

examples.en: You'd better mind your own business.

note: A reply to excessive curiosity from others.

meanings: typically Serbian ways, things that happen only in Serbia

examples.en: The bus is late - typical Serbia!

note: People also say «балканска посла» for things typical of the Balkans.

meanings: a Christmas greeting; the reply is «Ваистину се роди!»

examples.en: - Christ is born! - Truly he is born!

note: To simply wish someone well, say «Срећан Божић!». Orthodox Christmas in Serbia is on January 7.

meanings: a polite closing formula for a letter

examples.sr: Хвала на пажњи. [С пошто̀вањем], Марко Петровић.
examples.en: Thank you for your attention. Sincerely, Marko Petrović.

note: For informal cards: «с љубављу».

meanings: a warm sign-off on a card or letter

examples.sr: Срећна Нова година! [С љу̀бављу], твоја Ана.
examples.en: Happy New Year! With love, your Ana.

meanings: goes smoothly, like clockwork; of a drink, goes down easily
forms: literally: slides like a kitten down a gutter

examples.sr: Посао нам иде [ка̏о ма̏че ни̏з о̀лук].
examples.en: Our work is going like clockwork.
The rakija goes down easily.

note: Most often said of a drink that goes down without effort.

meanings: the area of Belgrade enclosed by the loop of tram line 2
forms: literally: the circle of the two

examples.en: I live inside the number 2 loop.

note: A line number is named with a feminine noun: двојка, тројка, петица, деветка. The same goes for trolleybus and bus lines.

meanings: a joke about bureaucracy: you're missing one more document
forms: literally: you are missing one paper

examples.sr: Жао ми је, [фа̏ли вам јѐдан па̀пӣр].
examples.en: I'm sorry, you're missing one more paper.

note: Abbreviated ФТЈП. You expect to hear it from the clerk at the counter when you think all the documents are collected.

examples.en: Thursday is neither here nor there.

note: People joke that Thursday is the middle of the week: «Четвртак - ни тамо ни овамо».

examples.en: He isn't easy to reach by phone.
Why didn't you call me back right away?

examples.sr: Није [глу̑п ка̏о ма̀гарац], само је ћутљив.
examples.en: He isn't stupid, he's just quiet.

note: The donkey also stands for stubbornness: «тврдоглав као магарац».

key: phr:моје срце куца само за тебе
forms: literally: my heart beats only for you

examples.sr: Љубави моја, [мо̀је ср̏це ку́ца са̏мо за те̏бе]!
examples.en: My love, my heart beats only for you!

note: Fits a card for Valentine's Day (February 14).

examples.en: I have to go, see you tomorrow!

note: Among friends, when you expect to meet soon.

meanings: talk to you later, we'll be in touch

examples.en: Thanks for the help, talk soon!

note: A very common goodbye when you want to stay in touch.

examples.en: Have a good trip, take care!

note: Concern for someone close; the polite form is «чувајте се».

examples.en: I'm going to bed, good night!

note: Also said as a farewell late in the evening.

examples.en: Have a good time at the seaside, enjoy!

note: A wish for someone who is about to do something pleasant. The polite form is «уживајте».

meanings: the relationship fell apart, the friendship is over

examples.sr: Били су другови, али је [пу̏кла ти̏ква].
examples.en: They were friends, but then it all fell apart.

note: Said when everything goes wrong after a quarrel.

meanings: I lost my patience, I snapped

examples.sr: Три сата у гужви и [пу̏као ми је фи̏лм].
examples.en: Three hours in a traffic jam, and I snapped.

note: A colloquial expression; the verb agrees with «филм».

meanings: to come apart at the seams, to fall apart
forms: literally: to burst at the seams

examples.sr: План ће [пу̏ћи по ша̀вовима] ако не нађемо решење.
examples.en: The plan will fall apart if we don't find a solution.

meanings: to fall apart, to break down, also emotionally
forms: literally: to burst like a rattle

examples.sr: Ауто је стар, једног дана ће [пу̏ћи ка̏о звѐчка].
examples.en: The car is old, one day it will fall apart.

examples.sr: У нашем крају има много паса [лу́талица].
examples.en: There are a lot of stray dogs in our neighborhood.

note: Plural: «пси луталице».
